title: The Body Communicates: An Integrative Guide to Ayurveda/Women’s Hormonal Health
description: When imbalances arise in a woman's body, it's not a sign that the body is malfunctioning—it's simply communicating. This presentation explores how the ancient wisdom of Ayurveda can be combined with modern Western medicine to guide women back to their natural equilibrium. We will look at how traditional principles can gently support the female body through major life transitions like menopause, perimenopause, and the journey of fertility. The discussion will highlight the deep connection between the nervous system, stress regulation, and cyclical well-being, addressing the areas where conventional care often leaves women looking for a more personal, root-cause approach. Participants will be guided through a compassionate framework designed to translate these holistic concepts into practical and gentle self-care routines. **Practicalities:** The event will take place at Kube Coworking, upstairs in the Open Hall. We will begin promptly at 6.30pm so please ensure that you are seated before then so as not to disrupt the energy of the event. You can buy refreshments at the adjoining cafe before the event. There is no charge for attendance but we recommend a voluntary donation of at least €5 (cash only) for those who are willing and able to contribute to help cover the use of the venue, support for the presenters, as well as administrative costs. If you have any questions about this event, please feel free to reach out to Kat LeRoy. **About the venue:** **Kübe** is a coworking space that supports engaged communities that align with our values—creativity, networking, learning, and well-being—by providing space for impactful events. **About the Presenter:** **Hannah Schmitt, MD,** is a German medical doctor, yoga teacher, and Ayurveda practitioner specializing in holistic women’s health, as well as the host of the German podcast Soma Talk. Her work is guided by the idea of careful listening, blending her clinical training from med school with advanced Ayurvedic and European herbal studies to support the body, mind, and soul. Hannah’s integrative approach focuses on gentle nervous system regulation and specialized hormonal and pre-/postnatal yoga to guide women through times of stress and hormonal transition. By bridging medical knowledge with a soft, embodied approach, she creates a safe space of trust where women can slow down, reconnect, and return to balance at their own natural pace.
